questions.q: An alternating voltage $V ( t ) = 220sin100\pit$ volt is applied to a purely resistive load of $50Ω$. The time taken for the current to rise from half of the peak value to the peak value is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time taken to change current value from half of the peak value to the peak value is,

$t = \dfrac{T}{6}$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{2\pi}{6\omega} = \dfrac{π}{3\omega} = \dfrac{π}{300\pi} = \dfrac{1}{300} = 3 . 33ms$

questions.q:
A series LCR circuit driven by $300V$ at a frequency of $50$ Hz contains a resistance $R = 3kΩ$, an inductor of inductive reactance ${X}_{L} = 250\piΩ$ and an unknown capacitor. The value of capacitance to maximise the average power should be:
\left(\text{take}{π}^{2} = 10\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular frequency,& $\omega = 2\pif = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pirads^{- 1}$

At resonance,

${X}_{C} = {X}_{L} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{ωC} = \omega L ⇒ \dfrac{1}{ωC} = 250\pi ⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{100\pi \times 250\pi}F = 4\mu F$

questions.q: A power transmission line feeds input power at $2300V$ to a step down transformer with its primary windings having $4000$ turns. The output power is delivered at $230V$ by the transformer. If the current in the primary of the transformer is $5A$ and its efficiency is $90%$, the output current would be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Efficiency $n = 90%$

$⇒ 0.9 \times powerin = Powerout$

$0.9 \times 2300 \times 5 = 230 \times {I}_{out}$

${I}_{out} = 45A$

questions.q: A& $750Hz, 20V  \left(rms\right)$ source is connected to a resistance of~$100Ω,$ an inductance of~$0 . 1803H$ and a capacitance of~$10\muF$ all in series. The time in which the resistance (heat capacity $2J / ° C$ ) will get heated by~$10 ° C . (assume no loss of heat to the surroundings) is close to :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The AC circuit is shown below.

Here,$R = 100, {X}_{L} = L\omega = 0 . 1803 \times 750 \times 2\pi = 850Ω$

The capacitive reactance~${X}_{c} = \dfrac{1}{Cω} = \dfrac{1}{{10}^{- 5} \times 2\pi \times 750} = 21 . 23Ω$

Total impedance~$Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2}$

$= \sqrt{{100}^{2} + \left(850 - 21 . 23\right)2} = 834 . 77 \approx 835$

The heat loss~$H = {i}_{rms}^{2}Rt = \left(ms\right) ∆ t$

$\dfrac{20}{835} \times \dfrac{20}{835} \times 100t = \left(2\right) \times 10$

$t = 348 . 61sec$

questions.q: A sinusoidal voltage $V\left(t\right) = 210sin3000t$ volt is applied to a series LCR circuit in which $L = 10mH, C = 25\mu F$ and $R = 100Ω$. The phase difference  \left(Φ\right)$& between the applied voltage and resultant current will be& $
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capacitive reactance is& ${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = \dfrac{1}{3000 \times 25 \times {10}^{- 6}} = \dfrac{40}{3}Ω$

Inductive reactance is~${X}_{L} = \omegaL = 3000 \times 10 \times {10}^{- 3} = 30Ω$

Now, total~reactance is~$X = {X}_{L} - {X}_{C}$

$= 30 - \dfrac{40}{3} = \dfrac{50}{3}Ω$

$tanϕ = \dfrac{X}{R} = \dfrac{\dfrac{50}{3}}{100} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$tanϕ = \dfrac{1}{6} = 0 . 17$

Hence, the phase difference between the applied voltage and resultant current is~$\tan^{- 1} \left(0 . 17\right).

$

B Transformer II Electromagnetic Induction

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) An AC generator works on the electromagnetic induction principle. So,& \left(A\right) \to II$

(B)~The transformer works on the principle of mutual induction.~So,~\left(B\right) \to IV$

(C)~Resonance occurs when the value of inductive and capacitive reactance have equal magnitude but a phase difference of $180 °$.~ So,~\left(C\right) \to I$

(D) The sharpness of resonance is defined using the quality~factor which explains how fast energy decay in an oscillating system.~\left(D\right) \to III$&

questions.q: A transformer operating at primary voltage $8kV$ and secondary voltage $160V$ serves a load of $80kW$. Assuming the transformer to be ideal with purely resistive load and working on unity power factor, the loads in the primary and secondary circuit would be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since the transformer is assumed to be purely resistive, the power of the transformer can be calculated with& $P = \dfrac{V2}{R}$. Therefore,

For the primary coil,

$P = \dfrac{\left(8 \times {10}^{3}\right)2}{RP} = 80 \times {10}^{3}W$

$⇒ {R}_{P} = 800Ω$

For the secondary coil,

$P = \dfrac{\left(160\right)2}{RS} = 80 \times {10}^{3}W$

$⇒ {R}_{S} = 0 . 32Ω$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Maximum power is dissipated in a circuit containing an inductor, a capacitor and a resistor connected in series with an $AC$ source, when resonance occurs.

Statement II: Maximum power is dissipated in a circuit containing pure resistor due to zero phase difference between current and voltage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for impedance is given by&

$Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2}$

At resonance,~${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$. So,~${Z}_\min = R$

Power will be maximum when impedance is minimum. Thus the maximum power occurs in a purely resistive circuit.&

questions.q: The primary side of a transformer is connected to $230V, 50Hz$ supply. The turn ratio of primary to secondary winding is $10: 1$. Load resistance connected to the secondary side is $46Ω$. The power consumed in it is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The voltages associated with the primary and the secondary side of the transformer are related to the turn ratio as follows:

$\dfrac{V1}{{V}_{2}} = \dfrac{N1}{{N}_{2}} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

\dfrac{230}{V2} = \dfrac{10}{1}

${V}_{2} = 23V$

Hence, the power consumed can be calculated as follows

\begin{cases}$P & = & {V}_{2}^{2}R \\ & = & $\dfrac{23 \times 23}{46}$\\ & = & 11 . 5W\end{cases}

$

questions.q: A series $AC$ circuit containing an inductor  \left(20mH\right),$ a capacitor \left(120\text{\mu}F\right)$ and a resistor  \left(60Ω\right)$ is driven by an $AC$ source of $24V / 50Hz .$ The energy dissipated in the circuit in $60s$ is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(Power factor), ${P}_{f} = cos ⁡ \text{ϕ} = \dfrac{R}{Z}$

Where~$R, Z$~are the resistance and impedance respectively.
(Energy dissipated)~$E = {V}_{rms}^{2}Z \times cos\text{ϕ} \times t$
$⇒ E = {V}_{rms}^{2}Z \times \dfrac{R}{Z} \times t$

$⇒ E = {V}_{rms}^{2}Z^{2} \times R \times t$

${V}_{rms}, t$~are the RMS voltage and time respectively.

We know that the Impedance of a~LCR circuit is given by the formula,
$Z^{2} = R^{2} + \left(\text{\omega}L - \dfrac{1}{\text{\omega}C}\right)2 ⇒ Z^{2} = {60}^{2} + \left(2\text{\pi} \times 50 \times 20 \times {10}^{- 3} - \left(\dfrac{1}{2\text{\pi} \times 50 \times 120 \times {10}^{- 6}}\right)\right)2$

Where~$\text{\omega}, L, C$~are the angular frequency, inductance and capacitance in the circuit respectively.
$⇒ Z^{2} = {60}^{2} + \left(2\text{\pi} - \dfrac{1000}{12\text{\pi}}\right)2$

$⇒ Z^{2} = 4009 . 7$

$∴ E = \dfrac{242}{4009 . 7} \times 60 \times 60J$~

$= 517 . 14J$

$= 5.17 \times {10}^{2}J$

questions.q:
As per the given graph, choose the correct representation for curve $A$ and curve $B$
{Where ${X}_{C} =$ Reactance of pure capacitive circuit connected with A.C. source
${X}_{L} =$ Reactance of pure inductive circuit connected with A.C. source
$R =$ Impedance of pure resistive circuit connected with A.C. source
$Z =$ Impedance of the $LCR$ series circuit }
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the inductive reactance is

${X}_{L} = \omegaL . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate capacitive reactance is

${X}_{C} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\omegaC}\right) . . . \left($2\right)$

As can be seen from equation (1), the inductive reactance varies directly with the frequency and equation (2) indicates that capacitive reactance varies inversely with the frequency.

Hence, curve~$A$~represents the capacitive reactance and curve~$B$ \text{ and } represents the inductive reactance.

$

questions.q: An inductor of $0 . 5mH$, a capacitor of $200\mu F$ and a resistor of $2Ω$ are connected in series with a $220V$ ac source. If the current is in phase with the emf, the frequency of ac source will be ______\times {10}^{2}Hz.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here:& $L = 0 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}H$

$C = 200 \times {10}^{- 6}F$

$R = 2Ω$.

If current is in phase with emf, so this is the condition of resonance.

$f = {f}_{R} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{2 \times 3 . 14\sqrt{LC}}$

$f = \dfrac{1}{6 . 28\sqrt{0 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 200 \times {10}^{- 6}}} = 503 . 55Hz = 5 . 03 \times {10}^{2}Hz$

questions.q: An AC& circuit has an inductor and a resistor of resistance $R$ in series, such that ${X}_{L} = 3R$. Now, a capacitor is added in series such that ${X}_{C} = 2R$. the ratio of the new power factor with the old power factor of the circuit is $\sqrt{5}: x$. The value of $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
First Recall the formula of power factor,& $cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z}⇒ cos{ϕ}_{initial} = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{R}{\left({X}_{L}\right)2 + R^{2}} = \dfrac{R}{9R^{2} + R^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{10}$.~

$⇒ cos{ϕ}_{final} = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{R}{\left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2 + R^{2}} = \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + R^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{cos{ϕ}_{final}}{cos{ϕ}_{initial}} = \dfrac{5}{x} ⇒ x = 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

Input power, ${P}_{i} = 2300 \times 5\text{watt}$

Output power, ${P}_{0} = 2300 \times 5 \times 0 . 9$

Now, we can write $η = \dfrac{Pout}{Pin} = \dfrac{{V}_{S}{I}_{S}}{{V}_{P}{I}_{P}}$
$⇒ 0 . 9 = \dfrac{230{I}_{S}}{2300 \times 5} ⇒ {I}_{S} = 45A .$

questions.q: A series LCR circuit is connected to an ac source of $220V, 50Hz$. The circuit contain a resistance $R = 100Ω$ and an inductor of inductive reactance ${X}_{L} = 79 . 6Ω$. The capacitance of the capacitor needed to maximize the average rate at which energy is supplied will be ______~$\mu F$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The average rate at which energy supplied i.e. power delivered is maximum in case of the resonance, therefore

${X}_{C} = {X}_{L}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = 79 . 6Ω$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{\omega \times 79 . 6} = \dfrac{1}{2\pif \times 79 . 6} = \dfrac{1}{100\pi \times 79 . 6} = 40\mu F$

Hence,~$C = 40\mu F$.
